messages:
maria: Customer 'NeonAI' reporting sudden spike of 502/504s for streaming hosted inference around 10:23 UTC. Happens only for long-lived streams (>120s) and only when request includes a large X-Customer-Meta header (~2KB). Attaching quick repro curl.

maria: ```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Customer-Meta: {"plan":"enterprise","billing":{...large json...}}" \n  --data-binary @/dev/null -N https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/stream
```

oliver: :eyes: I see a matching spike in envoy metrics at 10:23:20 UTC on frontdoor-gw-3 — downstream 502 count up ~180 in 2m. Any trace ids?

maria: Trace id from one failed request: trace=tr-7f1b2c. Downstream logs show upstream reset during TLS/handshake phase. Snippet: 

maria: ```
[2026-03-12T10:23:21.123Z] envoy frontdoor-gw-3 trace=tr-7f1b2c upstream: SSL handshake failed: tlsv1.3 alert internal error
[2026-03-12T10:23:21.124Z] envoy frontdoor-gw-3 trace=tr-7f1b2c sending 502 to client
```

deploy-bot: cert-rotation-job completed for frontdoor cluster at 2026-03-12T10:20:15Z (job id rot-2026-03).

sam: That timing is suspicious. Could be session ticket / session resumption break after rotation. Why would it affect ongoing streams though?

oliver: Hypothesis: clients start with a resumed session, then at some point downstream/upstream attempts a rehandshake or reconnect (idle window/keepalive) and the resumed ticket is rejected after rotation -> handshake fails mid-stream -> envoy returns 502.

maria: I can reproduce locally by streaming a slow payload with a big header. Steps:

maria: ```
# repro
curl --http2 -H "X-Customer-Meta: $(python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"big":"x"*1800}))')
     -v --limit-rate 10K -N https://staging-api.redwood/v1/stream
# wait ~2m
```

sam: In the upstream logs I'm seeing repeated: 

sam: ```
openssl: SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:internal error
upstream: close_notify or handshake failure
```

sam: Suggestion: try disabling TLS session tickets on a single frontdoor instance to confirm. If the error rate drops, it's session-resume related.

oliver: I can roll a config change to disable session tickets on frontdoor-gw-3 and enable ssl debug. Will do a canary roll.

deploy-bot: Rolling config change 'disable-tls-session-tickets' to frontdoor-gw-3 at 2026-03-12T10:29:05Z.

maria: Applied. Customer reports errors drop to near zero within 30s of the change. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime: Thanks — filing this into eng-runtime backlog as a postmortem item. Assigning to @oliver to investigate OpenSSL/OpenSSL config and session ticket handling with our cert-rotation flow. Also add an e2e that simulates large-header long-lived h2 streams during rotation.

maria: Created support ticket TS-8821, notified account team and the customer. For short-term mitigation we recommended client-side retry on 502 with exponential backoff and a 2nd-attempt that forces a fresh handshake.

oliver: I'll follow up with a deeper root cause analysis and a remediation plan (either change rotation to do graceful ticket invalidation, or ensure session ticket keys are compatible). Will post updates in this thread.

maria: Thanks all, closing the immediate escalation. We'll keep the support ticket open for the follow-up.
